To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
context-specific cognitive control effects in a modified flanker paradigm reflect adjustments in response criterion rather than in sensory evidence accumulation.

the CSPC effect is a context-specific effect that is not mediated by contextually enhanced processing selectivity but rather by contextually enhanced response caution, which is in turn mediated by the prediction error triggered by encountering rare events.

1) context-specific proportion congruency (CSPC; i.e., the congruency effect is larger in a frequent conflict context than in a rare conflict context) is a robust effect that is observed across a variety of tasks, 2) CSPC is mediated by adjustments of response caution (i.e., response criterion), and 3) CSPC is not mediated by adjustments of the rate of evidence accumulation (i.e., drift rate).

cognitive control is not a unitary process but rather a complex set of processes that may be triggered by different types of cues (i.e., context, conflict, prediction errors).
